The format, by example ​

What the file standard looks like in practice: the parts of an index, how sections layer, and a real archive opened up.

A Mosaic dataset is described by an index file (MosaicIndexFile) with four parts:

FieldPurpose
headerFormat version (MosaicVersion).
importsOther Mosaic files pulled in by URI, optionally pinned with an integrity hash.
componentTablesExternal component data — an NDJSON or Parquet file plus the schema of its rows.
sectionsThe actual content: provenance plus a list of nodes.

Each section carries a MosaicProvenanceHeader — who authored it, when, with which application, and a message describing the change — followed by the nodes it contributes. Because sections are a list, a dataset is a history of layered edits rather than a single flat snapshot.

A node has a uuid id and a list of component references. Each reference names a component type and identifies itself within the node with an id. Both remaining fields are optional: index points at a row of that type's table and defaults to -1, meaning the reference carries no value at all — a core::child or core::name says everything in its id, so its type needs no table. operation defaults to VALUE:

  • PASS_THROUGH — leave the inherited value alone
  • DELETE — unset the value
  • VALUE — set the value

That three-way operation is what lets a later section modify a node introduced by an earlier one without restating everything about it. Since VALUE is the default, a reference that sets something is written without an operation at all:

json
{ "type": "core::transform", "id": "transform", "index": 0 }
{ "type": "core::name", "id": "Left plinth" }
{ "type": "core::child", "id": "d6c1d2ba-9376-4461-8c56-27c496c1d2ba" }
{ "type": "core::child", "id": "66666666-6666-4666-8666-666666666666", "operation": "DELETE" }

Example: boxes by type ​

An archive is a zip holding index.json and one .ndjson table per component type. Here are the interesting parts of one: two type nodes and four nodes that are of those types, linked with core::inherit. The nodes carry a name, an is-a link and a placement — the mesh arrives through inheritance. The last tab is the whole source document it is packed from.

json
{
  "header": { "MosaicVersion": "post-alpha" },
  "componentTables": [
    { "filename": "core::transform.ndjson", "type": "NDJSON", "schema": { "…": "inlined" } }
  ],
  "sections": [{
    "header": {
      "id": "typed-boxes",
      "message": "Four boxes that inherit their shape from a type",
      "author": "ada@example.com",
      "timestamp": "2026-09-02T09:30:00Z"
    },
    "nodes": [
      {
        "id": "70000000-7000-4000-8000-700000000001",
        "components": [
          { "type": "core::name", "id": "Box type" },
          { "type": "khronos::gltf::meshPrimitive", "id": "mesh", "index": 0 },
          { "type": "core::transform", "id": "transform", "index": 0 }
        ]
      },
      {
        "id": "70000000-7000-4000-8000-700000000002",
        "components": [
          { "type": "core::name", "id": "Small box type" },
          { "type": "core::inherit", "id": "70000000-7000-4000-8000-700000000001" },
          { "type": "core::transform", "id": "transform", "index": 1 }
        ]
      },
      {
        "id": "70000000-7000-4000-8000-700000000003",
        "components": [
          { "type": "core::name", "id": "Near box" },
          { "type": "core::inherit", "id": "70000000-7000-4000-8000-700000000001" }, 
          { "type": "core::transform", "id": "transform", "index": 2 }
        ]
      }
    ]
  }]
}
json
{"translation":[0,2,0],"scale":[0.5,0.5,0.5]}
{"translation":[0,2,1.5],"scale":[0.25,0.25,0.25]}
{"translation":[-1,0,0]}
{"translation":[1,0,0]}
{"translation":[0,0,1.5]}
json
{
  "description": "Two type nodes and four things that are of those types. A core::inherit reference carries no value: its id is the node to inherit from, and composing gives the node every component of that node, except where it carries one under the same reference id, which wins. So 'Box type' holds the mesh once and everything that is-a box picks it up without restating it, while each one overrides the transform to say where it sits. 'Small box type' is-a box type in turn, overriding only the scale, which shows that inheritance follows a chain and that a middle link shields what it replaced. 'Unplaced box' overrides nothing, so it keeps the type's own transform. Unlike a core::child link, inheritance changes the node itself, so a query for everything that is-a box type has only to look at the nodes.",
